hook: BITS Hyderabad students pitch Army a radio at *1/5th* the import price
hook_b: BITS Hyderabad students pitch Army a radio at *1/5th* the import price
tldr: Krathveil, a startup by two 20-year-old BITS Pilani Hyderabad students, has built Krath Control, a sub-180 g radio that links soldiers over an encrypted mesh without towers, satellites or SIM cards. Two Army units have assessed it.

beats.what: Krath Control pairs with a soldier's phone and links to nearby radios in an encrypted mesh that reroutes if one node drops out.
beats.why: Conventional voice radios don't show locations, and imported live-map systems cost several times more and are closed systems, the founders say.
beats.care: Army units asked for power raised from 156 mW to 1 W and better antennas; an upgraded version is planned in 2-3 months.

effects.label: Army asks for 1 W power, better antennas

cards.title: 🆕 What's new
cards.body: TOI (Nov 17): An Army official said there is no Indian alternative today and called Krathveil's 'a promising one'.

cards.q: Would you join a student startup over a campus placement?

qs: What does an Army trial need to see before it buys an Indian device?
Can a 1 W radio hold the 100 km hops the founders describe?

facts.t: The radio weighs *under 180 grams* and needs no tower, satellite or SIM.
Founders say one hop between two hilltops can cover *more than 100 km* on paper.
It is at least the *second* BITS Hyderabad student startup to draw the Army, after drone-maker Apollyon Dynamics.

viz.verdict: Cheaper for the Army if the Indian device clears trials
Army's ask for the next version

learn.t: Mesh network = each device relays signals to its neighbours, so no tower is needed

watch: Whether the upgraded radio, due in two to three months, clears a second Army assessment.

sources.name: Times of India
sources.title: Army eyes cheaper pocket-sized radio built by BITS Hyderabad's students

fact: BITS Hyderabad students built a *₹40,000* pocket radio the Army is assessing
twist: The Army currently imports similar devices from the US at around ₹2 lakh apiece.
